blocks.text: Many decimal fractions have no exact binary floating-point representation.
math.isclose(a, b, rel_tol=..., abs_tol=...) uses relative and absolute tolerances instead of demanding exact equality.
The default relative tolerance is 1e-9 and absolute tolerance is 0.0; comparison to zero requires an appropriate positive absolute tolerance when nonzero differences should count as close.

blocks.code:
import math
print(0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3)
print(math.isclose(0.1 + 0.2, 0.3))
print(math.isclose(0.000001, 0.0, abs_tol=0.00001))

annotations.text: Near zero, the default absolute tolerance supplies no positive allowance.
Result: `False`; this computed sum is not exactly equal to 0.3.
Result: `True`; the values are close under the default tolerances.
Result: `True`; the explicit positive `abs_tol=0.00001` allows this difference from zero.

blocks.text: strip() removes leading and trailing whitespace, not whitespace inside the text.
The chars argument to strip describes removable edge characters, not a literal prefix or suffix.
lower() returns a copy with cased characters changed to lowercase.
With an explicit separator, split separates on that delimiter and keeps empty fields between repeated delimiters.
Without a separator, split() groups whitespace runs and omits leading and trailing empty fields.

left.code:
text = "  Blue  "
print(text.strip().lower())
print("xylabelyx".strip("xy"))
print("  red   blue  ".strip())

annotations.text: Strip removes edge whitespace, not interior whitespace. Lower returns a lowercase copy; strip chars are removable characters.
`text.strip()` returns `'Blue'`; applying `.lower()` returns `'blue'`.
`'xylabelyx'.strip('xy')` returns `'label'`: x and y are removable edge characters, not a literal affix.
Returns `'red   blue'`: the three interior spaces remain.
An explicit delimiter preserves empty fields between repeated delimiters; whitespace splitting groups runs and omits edge empty fields.
`'red,,blue'.split(',')` returns `['red', '', 'blue']`.
`'  red   blue  '.split()` returns `['red', 'blue']`.

tiles.title: Encoding and decoding Unicode text and bytes

steps.title: Encoding and decoding Unicode text and bytes

blocks.text: str holds Unicode text; bytes holds binary data. They are distinct kinds of values.
text.encode("utf-8") produces bytes using UTF-8.
Decode UTF-8 bytes with payload.decode("utf-8") to get text. Match the decoding encoding to the encoded data to recover that text.
Bytes invalid for the chosen decoding cause a decoding failure: UnicodeDecodeError.

blocks.code:
text = "café"
payload = text.encode("utf-8")
restored = payload.decode("utf-8")
print(type(text))
print(type(payload))
print(restored)
print(restored == text)

annotations.text: Encoded bytes are not already Unicode text.
`text` is the Unicode string `'café'`.
`payload` is the UTF-8 bytes value `b'caf\xc3\xa9'`, not a str.
Matching UTF-8 decoding restores `'café'`.
The displayed types are `<class 'str'>` and `<class 'bytes'>`.
Displays `café`.
Displays `True`: restored text equals the original text.
